subject: Linear mixed model with crossed factors. help with algebra

messages.author: 146a54acf88740fd
messages.subject: Linear mixed model with crossed factors. help with algebra
parts:
Hi to everybody.
I am rather new to brms and I would like to use brms as a tool to improve my modelling skill in stan.
Writing stan code is ok for me when I have simple models, with more complex models I prefer to use brms because model specification is easy and I get my results quickier.
However brms has spoiled me a bit: I would like to extend my models (adding kalman filtering, or gaussian process) writing the stan code by my own.

So I decided to start from the very basis: I am now trying to write down a simple mixed model (random intercept).
For one site the daily average temperature (TAVG) has been measured and I would like to find the climatic average daily temperature for each day of the year (DOY = 1:366).

This is the model I have written by my own:
data {
    int<lower=1> N;
    int<lower=1> J; //J = 366
    vector[N] y;
    int<lower=1, upper=J> DOY[N];
}

parameters {
    vector[J] mu_day;  //daily climatic average temperature
    real mu_year;   //yearly climatic average temperature
    real<lower=0> sigma_year;
    real<lower=0> sigma_day;
}

transformed parameters {
    vector[N] mu_day_hat;
   
    mu_day_hat = mu_day[DOY];
}

model {
    sigma_year ~ cauchy(0, 5);
    mu_year ~ normal(6.5, 1);
    mu_day ~ normal(mu_year, sigma_year);
    y ~ normal(mu_day_hat, sigma_day);
}


With brms the same model should be stated as TAVG ~ 1+ (1|DOY) 

However if I look to the stan code generated by brms,  the data section states:

data {
  int<lower=1> N;  // total number of observations
  vector[N] Y;  // response variable
  // data for group-level effects of ID 1
  int<lower=1> J_1[N];
  int<lower=1> N_1;
  int<lower=1> M_1;
  vector[N] Z_1_1;
  int prior_only;  // should the likelihood be ignored?
}

where
J_1 is the vector oif the DOY indicator
N_1 and M_1 are used to define the group level standard deviation and the unscaled group-level effects.

I tried to retro engineer the machinery of the calculation of the model section:

vector[N] mu = rep_vector(0, N) + temp_Intercept;
  for (n in 1:N) {
    mu[n] = mu[n] + (r_1_1[J_1[n]]) * Z_1_1[n];
  }

but until now I could not figure out the algebra behind the model. Because I can't figure out how Z_1_1 is made.

Where can I find the definition of the general structure of the matrices used for this kind of problems?

Thanks in advance

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Linear mixed model with crossed factors. help with algebra
parts:
For a random intercept model, Z_1_1 is just a vector containing 1s. ;-)

Please see make_standata to get the data corresponding to the Stan code produced by make_stancode.

Best,
Paul
